title: The Context of Our Character, Part 1
coreMove: Move the honesty cue to the moment before rationalization starts.
sourcePressure: The source focuses on small dishonesty, self-concept maintenance, and the way timely moral reminders such as honor codes reduce cheating before temptation is rationalized.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says people cheat when they can; the exact lesson is that context changes how much cheating still feels compatible with being honest.

hook: Small lies keep a clean mirror

exampleSpecs.domain: charity raffle ticket counting after a fundraiser
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer treasurer reconciling cash and unsold ticket stubs
exampleSpecs.stakes: rounding in her own favor while still feeling like a good volunteer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before counting cash, the treasurer reads the posted donor pledge aloud and initials the count sheet beside another volunteer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: raffle stubs spread across a folding table after the hall lights come up

exampleSpecs.domain: farmers market honor jar for flower bouquets
exampleSpecs.audience: a stall owner testing a payment setup when she steps away
exampleSpecs.stakes: customers shaving a dollar while still seeing themselves as honest neighbors
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner moves a simple honesty note from behind the jar to eye level before the first customer takes a bouquet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an honor jar beside wrapped flower bouquets under a striped awning

exampleSpecs.domain: library self-checkout for rare local-history folders
exampleSpecs.audience: an archivist worried about patrons skipping sign-out steps
exampleSpecs.stakes: folders going missing because the act feels too minor to count as dishonesty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the archivist places the handling oath on top of the folder box, so patrons touch it before removing a folder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cream-colored archive folders in a gray box beneath a cotton handling sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: youth soccer referee assigning final score reports
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer referee entering scores after a disputed match
exampleSpecs.stakes: softening a yellow-card report because one team is local and the lie feels small
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the referee reads the fairness line at the top of the score form before filling in the card count
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp score form clipped to a fence after a muddy match

exampleSpecs.audience: a member logging laser-cutter minutes after a late session
exampleSpecs.stakes: underreporting use because nobody was watching and the extra minutes feel harmless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after discrepancies appear, the shop moves the member agreement above the time keypad and asks members to tap it before entering minutes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laser-cutter keypad glowing beside a stack of acrylic offcuts

exampleSpecs.audience: a conference organizer preventing inflated attendance claims
exampleSpecs.stakes: attendees claiming credit for sessions they left early while preserving a professional self-image
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after moving the professional attestation above the session checklist, claimed credits drop without extra policing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a badge lanyard lying across a continuing-education checklist

skillTargets: place moral reminders before the decision
distinguish character labels from context design
evaluate whether a cue protects self-concept at the right moment

tryThisNowSpec: Move one rule, pledge, or standard from after-the-fact review to the exact place where the questionable choice begins.
